title: Integration with Azure Static Web Apps from Business Central
summary: This post explains how to integrate an Azure Static Web App with Business Central by using the WebPageViewer control add-in and the window.postMessage API to enable bidirectional communication between AL code and a hosted web application.
key_points: WebPageViewer control add-in shows hosted web content inside an iframe on a Business Central page
window.postMessage carries messages both ways between AL code and the embedded web app
AL side calls SubscribeToEvent with the expected origin, Navigate to the URL, PostMessage to send, and handles replies in the Callback trigger
Web app listens with addEventListener for message events and replies via window.parent.postMessage with a target origin
The app must be served over SSL; with a self-signed emulator certificate it loaded but could not send messages back to BC, which worked once deployed to Azure Static Web Apps

quotes.text: This is the scenario that we have on the BC web client page. The WebPageViewer control add in loads its content inside an iframe.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the core architecture where the web app runs in an iframe context, enabling message-based communication with AL code
